title: Armstrong's favourite step and Peg Leg Bates teaching him
summary: Green says Armstrong recognised his new tap degree, and Peg Leg Bates taught him a step and made him repeat it, which began their friendship.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: "Satchmo" Armstrong, and quite a few others, you know, but he was about the most important one to recognize the difference in the tap dancing, you see, because I was always trying to -- I introduced a new degree into tap dancing from the fraternity and John Bubbles' teachings, you see. Mr. Peg Leg Bates -- he taught me a step that was a favorite of mine and I asked him was I doing it correctly? And evidently he liked to see me do the dance step, see. It was from the One Leg Dancing Fool, you see. He would make me repeat the step over and over and over again, you know, then he -- finally he would say, "Yes, you did it better," he'd shout, "Next time I see you, I want to see you do it the way it should be did," you know. So, that's how we became friends.
